speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and have they changed in size or appearance since they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions flat-topped, smooth, and flesh-colored or pinkish in appearance? Have you noticed any central dimpling or umbilication on the tops of these papules?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST IMAGES
Given the classic presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules and exposure to another child with similar lesions, I am highly suspicious of Molluscum Contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
